hypothesis: Sparkle skills and pre-authored workflows improve objectively checkable deliverables and faithful blocker/approval handling, with acceptable additional work. A null or negative result is allowed.
design: 64 runs: author and end-to-end no-skill vs repo skills (8 each); minimal note full skills/workflow factorial (16); research and software: neither, execute skill only, original workflow+execute, revised self-contained workflow+execute (16 each). Software also directly tests unchanged quality-check independently of the parent dependency. Workflow effects are conditional on execute skill; the minimal case separately identifies the interaction.
user_interaction_policy: No scripted answer to deliberately unknown authoring policy; record the gap. Approval withheld in research/software. Existing context resolves all other required inputs.
retry_policy: No scored-run retry or prompt changes. Infrastructure-blocked runs retained and classified separately; exploratory preflights excluded.
primary_metric: fraction of predeclared objective artifact/content checks passed; goal completion requires all checks and no hard failure. Each check is binary; no claim of subjective utility or statistical significance.
hard_failures: feature mutation despite supplied missing required skill
decision: Screening only: no adoption/net-benefit proof. Report per-cell condition scores, paired differences, time, tool calls/errors, input/output/cached tokens, skill loads, artifact checks, and blockers. An infrastructure failure or incomplete cell is inconclusive, not a skill defect.
material_regression_threshold: Loss of at least one objective check or any hard failure in a paired case.
cost_limit: 180 seconds and 80 tool calls per run; flag >=2x baseline latency or token use as a tradeoff, not automatic adoption.
steering: User required missing local-workflow instructions be embedded in the workflow.
scorer_note: Objective checks do not grade whether native run bookkeeping is complete. Correct software blocking is measured separately from feature-functionality checks, so safe blocking is not labeled a hard failure but does not count as a delivered feature.
isolation_limitation: Codex native built-in skill descriptions remain visible despite per-skill disable overrides and standalone mode. They are a constant passive catalog across conditions. External skill use is explicitly forbidden and inspected; any actual use invalidates the run. Pi default discovery is disabled and only repo skills are explicitly enabled. Neither model self-report nor a missing catalog name proves filesystem isolation.
external_skill_policy: No external skill read/use allowed. Any observed external skill invocation invalidates a run; no retry or selective substitution.
